> CRICSCORE is a portable, handheld cricket scoring console designed like a modern gaming device. It allows users to score cricket matches ball by ball using physical buttons or a connected phone, without requiring an internet connection. The device records runs, wickets, extras, overs and individual player statistics, storing all match data locally. When an internet connection becomes available, the recorded match can be synchronised with a companion website, which automatically generates an interactive scorecard featuring batting and bowling statistics, over-by-over timelines, run progression graphs, partnerships and match summaries. With its colour touchscreen, tactile scoring buttons, wireless connectivity and rechargeable battery, CRICSCORE aims to make cricket scoring convenient, accurate and accessible for international, school, club and local matches.

## Design

### 2026-11-01: Started the software development phase of CRICSCORE, my offline-first handheld cricket scoring device designed primarily for school, tennis-ball and neighbourhood cricket.

**15h**

Started the software development phase of CRICSCORE, my offline-first handheld cricket scoring device designed primarily for school, tennis-ball and neighbourhood cricket.

The first step was to plan the complete software architecture and establish the project structure. I outlined the different files, folders and modules required to build the system, separating the firmware, website and camera functionality so that each component can be developed and tested independently.

The planned project structure includes three major parts:

1. Main ESP32-S3 Firmware

Setting up the main controller and its software architecture.

Developing the cricket scoring engine for runs, wickets, overs and extras.

Implementing match creation, team and player management.

Planning batting and bowling statistics.

Adding undo and score-editing functionality.

Implementing offline match storage and recovery.

Creating a Wi-Fi access point and REST API for communication with the website.

Planning integration with the touchscreen and physical scoring buttons.

2. Companion Website

Planning the website dashboard and match management interface.

Designing the live scoring screen.

Outlining detailed batting and bowling scorecards.

Planning over-by-over timelines and run progression graphs.

Adding match history, analytics and match summaries.

Preparing the website to communicate directly with the ESP32 through its API.

Planning a responsive interface that works on both phones and computers.

3. ESP32-CAM Livestreaming Module

Planning a separate firmware project for the ESP32-CAM.

Setting up communication between the camera module and the main ESP32-S3.

Planning an MJPEG livestream endpoint.

Designing a livestream interface within the companion website.

Adding camera connection status and streaming controls.

After completing the initial architecture and file outline, I moved on to coding the different components. I have started implementing the ESP32 firmware, setting up the scoring logic and API structure, and laying the foundation for the companion website and camera integration.

I am currently approximately halfway through the initial coding phase. The main focus now is to get the different software components working together, establish reliable communication between the controllers and website, and ensure that the scoring system works correctly even without an internet connection.

Current Progress: Project architecture and file structure completed; initial software implementation underway, approximately 50% complete.

### 2026-11-01: Successfully completed the development of CRICSCORE, my offline-first handheld cricket scoring system, as part of Hack Club Half Life.

**9h**

Successfully completed the development of CRICSCORE, my offline-first handheld cricket scoring system, as part of Hack Club Half Life.

The project involved planning and developing the complete software structure, including the ESP32-S3 firmware, companion website, cricket scoring engine, communication APIs and ESP32-CAM livestreaming module.

I worked on implementing the core scoring features, match management, player statistics, extras handling, offline data storage and communication between the hardware and website. I also developed the website interface to display live scores, detailed scorecards, match statistics and analytics, alongside a dedicated interface for the camera livestream.

Completing this project has been a valuable learning experience. It allowed me to explore embedded programming, web development, hardware-software communication, wireless networking and system integration while building something based on a problem I have personally experienced.

With the development phase now complete, I am looking forward to submitting CRICSCORE and sharing the final outcome. It has been exciting to take an idea from the initial planning stage to a complete software implementation, and I hope to bring the physical device to life next.

Final Status: Software development completed. Ready for submission!
